title: 'fix(axis): refactor axisLabel formatter'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A chart author using custom axis label values needs labels to stay aligned with the same ordinal position they supplied, even when some custom values are filtered out because they fall outside the visible axis extent. Right now the formatter callback can receive the wrong index for repeated values because the label-building path looks the position back up from the filtered tick list instead of preserving the mapped position directly.


  ## Desired outcome

  When ECharts builds axis labels from `axisLabel.customValues`, the formatter should be called with the actual index of each rendered item in that filtered label sequence, including cases where the same numeric value appears more than once. Authors should be able to rely on formatter logic that branches on the index parameter without seeing duplicated values collapse onto the first matching position.


  ## Acceptance signals

  For duplicate or repeated custom label values that remain in range, each rendered label keeps its own formatter index and produces the text a user would expect from its own slot in the sequence. Existing axis label rendering behavior, formatter signatures, and label text generation outside this indexing bug remain unchanged.

  '
-----
title: 'fix(axis): fix chart does not work when using `customValues` with `formatter` in time axis label'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Time axes can break when authors combine `axisLabel.customValues` with a custom `axisLabel.formatter`, even though that pairing is a reasonable way to build bespoke label sets.

  ## Desired outcome

  Time-axis label generation should support `customValues` and formatter callbacks together without crashing or dropping the axis.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A time axis that uses both `axisLabel.customValues` and `axisLabel.formatter` renders normally and passes the formatter the expected label values.

  '

content.text: I verified the exact upstream change. Here is the plan.

input.summary: When `axisLabel.customValues` is set, `createAxisLabels` currently invokes the label formatter with only the tick object, so a user formatter `function (value, index)` receives `undefined` for `index`. The change must pass the position of each displayed custom tick as the second argument to the formatter, so formatters can build labels from the tick's position in the custom value sequence. No new public option or type change is needed — the formatter signatures in `axisCommonTypes.ts` already declare `index: number`.
steps: No signature/type changes are required. `makeLabelFormatter` in src/coord/axisHelper.ts already returns `(tick: ScaleTick, idx?: number) => string` (line 239) and its value/log branch already forwards `idx` to the user callback at lines 274-287: `return (labelFormatter as AxisLabelValueFormatter)(getAxisRawValue<false>(axis, tick), idx, extra);`. The public formatter types `AxisLabelValueFormatter` / `AxisLabelCategoryFormatter` / `AxisLabelTimeFormatter` in src/coord/axisCommonTypes.ts lines 240-254 already declare `index: number`. Do NOT add a new option and do NOT touch `axisHelper.ts`.
Do NOT change `createAxisTicks` (src/coord/axisTickLabelBuilder.ts lines 154-174). It has no formatter; `axisTick.customValues` is unaffected by this requirement.

Optional but matches the upstream PR (commit e192f497 "test: added a test case"): add a manual visual test to /workspace/test/axisLabel.html. Add `
` after line 48 (`
`), and append a new `` (line 481, before `` at line 482) that builds a `type: 'value'` xAxis with `axisTick.customValues: [100, 183, 218, 333, 478]`, `axisLabel.customValues: [100, 183, 218, 333, 478]` and `axisLabel.formatter: function (val, index) { return xLabels[index].toString(); }` where `xLabels = xValues.map(x => x * 5)`, rendered via `testHelper.create(echarts, 'main7', {title: 'Should be able to use index for custom values of axis label', option})`. Expected rendered labels: 500, 915, 1090, 1665, 2390.

Verification (no unit-test file exists for this area — /workspace/test/ut/spec has no coord/ or axis specs). The cheapest programmatic check follows the pattern in /workspace/test/ut/spec/scale/interval.test.ts lines 94-99: create a chart, then `(getECModel(chart).getComponent('xAxis', 0) as CartesianAxisModel).axis.getViewLabels().map(item => item.formattedLabel)`. With `xAxis: {type: 'value', axisLabel: {customValues: [0, 4, 7, 8, 9], formatter: (v, i) => i + ':' + v}}` the result must be `['0:0','1:4','2:7','3:8','4:9']` instead of the current `['undefined:0', ...]`. `Axis.getViewLabels` is at src/coord/Axis.ts:242-247 and delegates to `createAxisLabels`.

1. Sibling requirement `requirements/axislabel-formatter-indexing.yaml` ("fix(axis): refactor axisLabel formatter") is the *follow-up* to this exact commit (upstream 921496a2). It replaces `const index = ticks.indexOf(numval);` with the map callback index, i.e. `zrUtil.map(ticks, (numval, index) => {...})`, because `indexOf` returns the first match and therefore collapses duplicate custom values onto the same index. If you prefer the strictly-more-correct form, `zrUtil.map(ticks, (numval, index) => { const tick = {value: numval}; return { formattedLabel: labelFormatter(tick, index), ... }; })` is behaviourally identical for this requirement (all non-duplicate customValues) and additionally fixes duplicates — but it pre-implements the sibling task. The literal upstream diff for THIS requirement is the `ticks.indexOf(numval)` version.

2. Sibling requirement `requirements/time-axis-customvalues-formatter.yaml`: on a **time** axis, a *function* `axisLabel.formatter` combined with `customValues` still throws before and after this change, because `leveledFormat` (src/util/time.ts lines 331-352) does `level: tick.time.level` while the custom tick built here is only `{value: numval}` (no `time`). Do not try to fix that here; just do not write a time-axis test for this requirement.

3. **Category axes are unaffected by design.** `makeLabelFormatter` (src/coord/axisHelper.ts lines 257-272) ignores the `idx` argument for `axis.type === 'category'` and instead passes `tick.value - axis.scale.getExtent()[0]`, with an explicit back-compat comment. So `xAxis: {type: 'category', axisLabel: {customValues: [...], formatter: (v, i) => ...}}` will still receive the ordinal index, not the sequence position. Do not change that branch — it would be a breaking change. Test with a `value`/`log` axis.

4. Time-axis index offset: `tickValuesToNumbers` (lines 111-121) sorts and duplicates the first and last entry for `axis.type === 'time'`, so on time axes the index passed will be shifted relative to the user's `customValues` array. Upstream did not address this in this commit.

5. `ticks.indexOf` is native `Array.prototype.indexOf` (ES5) — allowed here; no eslint restriction exists in /workspace/.eslintrc-common.yaml. `zrUtil.indexOf(ticks, numval)` is the more idiomatic echarts helper if lint complains.

6. There is a duplicate-looking requirement pair (`axislabel-formatter-index.yaml` vs `axislabel-formatter-indexing.yaml`); make sure the commit for this task touches only the single call site in `createAxisLabels`.
